towns.name: Marshall County

reporting.basis: Actual results (as reported to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of Local Government Finances)
reporting.scope: All county funds, including the sheriff, jail, courts and county roads

ledger.counterparty: Annual Survey of Local Government Finances
Annual Survey of Local Government Finances

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau, 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, individual unit file
U.S. Census Bureau 2025 population estimates
U.S. Census Bureau 2024 Gazetteer (map location)
EFF Atlas of Surveillance (police surveillance technology, searched by department)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Debt service leaves out $186,000 of principal repaid with new borrowing the county did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Kansas county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-12. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Kansas yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
